subject: Threeway SKU band split and fallback guardrails for cloud marketplaces
messages:
From: aws-marketplace@amazon.com
To: kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: initial sync - SKU bands for ACME AI listing

Kimberly — thanks for the quick call yesterday. We want to draft a pragmatic initial listing that maps to three SKU bands (Entry/Standard/Enterprise) across AWS regions. Two asks from our side: 1) confirm which SKU maps to a marketplace metered usage model vs. a subscription SKU, and 2) a fallback policy if a region is out of capacity (preferred cross-cloud fallback?).

Attaching a short template if helpful. Can you put together an initial proposal by EOD Monday?

--
AWS Marketplace Partnerships
aws-marketplace@amazon.com
From: kimberly.park@redwood.com

Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-03T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Threeway SKU band split and fallback guardrails for cloud marketplaces

Thanks — looping in the product/ops leads so we can propose a concrete mapping. High-level constraints from Redwood: 
- We support both per-token metered and subscription SKUs; metered works best on hosted API where we can emit detailed usage records.
- For Dedicated/Private customers we normally offer subscription or committed capacity SKUs.

I'll circulate a short matrix (Entry/Std/Ent) with recommended region coverage and an initial fallback policy (cross-cloud fallback to GCP or Azure when allowed by customer). Posting draft in ~2 hours.

Kim
Kimberly Park
Director, GTM Operations | Redwood Inference
From: marissa.cole@redwood.com

Cc: connor.obrien@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-03T13:14:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Threeway SKU band split and fallback guardrails for cloud marketplaces

Adding operational notes for the matrix draft — please include these columns:
- SKU ID (internal)
- Offer type (metered/subscription/commit)
- Default region set (US East, US West)
- Fallback priority (same-cloud zone -> same-cloud region -> cross-cloud region)
- Can a customer opt-out of cross-cloud fallback? (Yes/No)
- Pricing band guidance (monthly list)

Also: recommend we carve out an "escape hatch" for large enterprise deals where we can do a private subscription in the customer's preferred cloud and remove them from marketplace routing. I'll add sample pricing buckets to the spreadsheet.

M
From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Cc: connor.obrien@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-04T09:07:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Threeway SKU band split and fallback guardrails for cloud marketplaces

Quick technical tradeoffs to surface for the matrix:
- Latency SLOs: Entry SKU should only include regions where average median p99 token latency < 250ms for typical gen workloads. Standard can accept up to 350ms with caching. Enterprise should include high-availability regions + Dedicated pools.
- Cost delta: cross-cloud fallback adds egress and operational overhead; recommend marking fallback-enabled SKUs with a +10-25% pricing adjustment or a separate SKU for fallback-enabled offers.
- KV cache sharing: cross-cloud fallbacks cannot share runtime caches, so warmed prefixes won't carry over — call this out as potential UX/regression.

I'll review the spreadsheet and add latency/cost columns.

Rishi
Senior Product Manager, Serving Runtime
From: gcp-partners@google.com
To: kimberly.park@redwood.com
Cc: aws-marketplace@amazon.com; marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-05T08:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Threeway SKU band split and fallback guardrails for cloud marketplaces

Appreciate the draft guidance. A couple of asks from GCP:
- For Enterprise SKUs we need explicit entitlements per region (e.g., us-central1, us-east4) to enable co-sell approvals. Can you enumerate zone/region granularity per SKU?
- We also want the canary fallback scenarios documented (when marketplace routing fails, what consumer-visible text and fallback path is shown).

We'll review once you upload the spreadsheet. Also looping in ACME purchasing to confirm whether they permit cross-cloud fallback for compliance reasons.

Thanks
GCP Marketplace Partnerships
From: kimberly.park@redwood.com
To: aws-marketplace@amazon.com; gcp-partners@google.com; purchasing@acme-ai.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, connor.obrien@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-05T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Final: SKU band matrix + fallback guardrails (upload + next steps)

Team — uploaded the first-pass matrix and canary scenarios to Drive (links below) and attached XLS/PDF copies. Key decisions captured: 
- Banding: Entry (metered, limited region set), Standard (metered + subscription, broad US coverage), Enterprise (subscription/commit, full US+EU coverage).
- Fallback policy: default same-cloud region fallback enabled; cross-cloud fallback is opt-in per customer and marked as a separate "Fallback-Enabled" SKU. Pricing delta recommended +20% when fallback-enabled.
- Canary behavior: consumer sees a polite notice "Switching to backup region to maintain availability" and logs a marketplace routing fallback event for billing reconciliation.

Action items: 
1) AWS/GCP partners to confirm region granularity for Enterprise entitlements by EOD Tuesday.
2) ACME Procurement to confirm whether cross-cloud fallback is permitted for their account (purchasing@acme-ai.com).
3) Product to add latency/cost columns and finalize price bands (marissa/rishi).

Attachments: sku-band-mapping-v1.xlsx, canary-fallback-scenarios.pdf
Drive: https://drive.redwood.com/teams/marketplace/sku-band-mapping-v1
